intent_en: To illustrate the dramatic increase in the share of profits that major American companies allocate to stock buybacks from 1982 to 2018.
previous_intent: To illustrate the dramatic increase in the share of profits spent on stock buybacks by major American companies from 1982 to 2018.
narration_support: spent less than 1 % of their profits on stock buybacks. By 2008, just before the recession, that share had jumped to 77%.
chart_support: Line chart showing 'Share of profits spent on stock buybacks' for S&P 500, displaying a sharp increase from 1982 to a peak in 2008 and remaining high in 2018.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly describes the jump from under 1% to 77% and 65%, while the chart visualizes this sharp upward trend in buyback spending relative to profits.
